messages:
Mia: quick heads-up, running the new python quickstart async sample and it hangs when the token refresh hits.
Devon: can you share a short repro or trace?
Mia: paste of the relevant bits below, simplified:
```python
# main.py
from sdk import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()  # created at import time

async def fetch():
    client.headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {get_token()}'  # get_token is sync (requests.post)
    await client.get('/v1/embeddings')
```

stack snippet shows httpx internals calling sync code on the event loop thread.
Ben: that pattern will block. Sync refresh inside an async flow ends up running in threadpool and can deadlock depending on how the loop/threadpool are started. Also creating AsyncClient at import time risks event loop mismatch with uvicorn/workers.
Olivia: +1. Another gotcha: our SDK retry middleware calls the auth callback on 401. If the callback is sync it gets wrapped into nested executor calls.
Mia: ugh, blame the quickstart; it copied the sync helper. I'm testing swapping to an async refresh now.
Sam: can you open a GH issue with a small repro and link the sample-apps PR? I can triage.
Mia: filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/2507 with a tiny repro and run log.
Devon: proposal: add an AsyncAuth helper in the SDK exposing a simple interface: async def refresh_token() -> str, internal asyncio.Lock to dedupe concurrent refreshes, and a sync shim for backwards compat. Also update quickstarts to show proper FastAPI/uvicorn startup usage (create AsyncClient in startup and close in shutdown).
Ben: also add a mypy/typing test: right now some async methods are annotated in a way that encourages sync wrappers (mypy thinks return is Response instead of Awaitable[Response]). That contributed to people writing sync helpers.
Olivia: I'll create an internal task to update all sample apps to use startup-scoped AsyncClient, provide an example AsyncAuth, and add a CI check that runs the async quickstart under uvicorn to catch deadlocks.
ci-bot: created issue #2507, triggered sample-apps CI run 5123.
Mia: confirmed: switching to an async refresh (await httpx.AsyncClient().post) + creating client inside startup resolved the hang locally. thanks.
Devon: nice. Ben/Olivia, want to coordinate docs and a small devex note about common sync/async pitfalls so folks don't copy sync snippets into async samples?
Ben: on it. I'll draft a short blurb and include code comparisons and the Lock pattern for deduping refreshes.
Mia: saving the repro and the fix notes to the issue. If anyone else hits event-loop mismatch ping me.
